content:
sam: quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100 focusing on max_tokens_per_batch and max_batch_size. attaching highlights and a tiny table.

maya: awesome. did you run with kv-cache enabled? that's usually the biggest variable.

sam: yes — two modes: KV on (persist across requests) and KV off (cold start each request). KV on shows better throughput but higher p95 in some kernels.

chris: can you paste the small summary table?

sam: sure — raw CSV:
```
gpu,workload,max_batch,max_tokens,median_ms,p95_ms,kv_mode,kernel
A10,chat-16k,8,16384,18.5,54.2,on,sel-v2
T4,chat-8k,6,8192,24.1,68.7,off,sel-v1
L4,chat-4k,10,4096,12.3,39.8,on,sel-v2
A100,chat-16k,16,16384,9.8,29.0,on,sel-v3
H100,chat-32k,32,32768,11.2,38.5,on,sel-v3
```

sam: interesting bit — H100 p95 increased by ~12% after pushing a kernel selector patch that changed how we pack KV pages. suspect kernel sel-v3 alignment with our KV sharding logic.

maya: hmm. does sel-v3 change paging/striding? that would impact KV hit locality.

sam: yes, it switched from 64B to 256B tile alignment for the GEMM kernel and also started using a different shared memory tiling. Latency impact shows up for long-tail requests where batch forms with mixed seq lengths.

lucy: any difference when we force token-limited batching vs fixed-batch-size? i.e., prefer max_tokens cap over N per batch.

sam: great question — we ran both strategies. token-limited batching (limit tokens/batch to 262k) reduced p95 on T4 and L4 by 8-10% vs fixed batch size, but on H100 it helped only when KV off. With KV on the CPU-side prefix caching and kernel change caused worse packing leading to +5-10% p95.

priya: is this a regression in the runtime or acceptable tradeoff? what's the cost delta?

sam: cost delta minimal for A10/T4/L4 (throughput improved), but for H100 the throughput stayed similar while p95 grew — customer-facing SLO risk. We measured token cost per request and saw ~2% higher GPU cycles for H100 for the same token budget.

chris: any quick mitigations? revert kernel sel-v3? or change queue policy to prefer single-length batching for H100?

sam: options:
- revert sel-v3 on H100 only (can gate by device_id)
- force token-limited batches + prefer homogeneous seq-length packing for H100 queues
- tweak KV page alignment code: revert tile size change or add an alignment shim
- lower max_batch_size for H100 when KV on to avoid bad packing

maya: I vote for a targeted revert for H100 while we instrument deeper. we should also add a regression unit test that simulates mixed seq-length batches with KV on.

lucy: agree. also add a runtime flag to prefer `tokens_per_batch` over `max_batch_size` per device.

sam: noted. I'll open a PR to gate sel-v3 by device and add a toggle. minimal rolling deploy to canary first.

priya: can you include the profiling flamegraphs? we need call stacks where latency jumps.

sam: attaching snippets (abbreviated):
```
H100: hot path
- kv_lookup() 35%
- kernel_sel_v3_pack() 28%
- run_gemm_tile() 15%
- scheduling/queue_overhead 12%
```

sam: follow-ups / owners:
- sam: gate sel-v3 on H100 (PR + canary) — ETA today EOD
- maya: add regression harness for KV+mixed-batches — ETA 2d
- lucy: runtime flag per-device tokens_vs_batch policy + docs — ETA 3d
- chris: measure cost delta for gated revert vs flag — ETA 2d

infra-bot: Deploy started: rolling canary to 2 H100 nodes (deploy_id: d-8231)

maya: ping when canary metrics are in, i'll run A/B of token-limited vs fixed on the canary cluster.

sam: will post metrics; preliminary canary shows p95 back to baseline on those 2 nodes (small sample). still need larger sweep.

lucy: couple notes for release notes: mention H100-specific kernel gating and new per-device tokens_vs_batch config. keep wording conservative.

priya: thanks team. good catch. let's not forget to run endpoint-level SLIs after deploy.

chris: added a short Jira: INF-4129 "H100 kernel sel-v3 gate + tokens_vs_batch policy" and linked PRs.

sam: closing loop — will update here when PR merges. thx :shipit:
